opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alexandra Johnson (employee ID E003) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E003.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Employee E003 (Alexandra Johnson), Analyst, full-time. Requested admin to Source Code. Full-time employees max out at write unless their role owns the system; Analyst does not own Source Code (Engineer does). Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Employee E003 (Alexandra Johnson), contractor, basic security training. Requested admin to Source Code. Contractors get read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Basic training maxes at read. Recommend read.
reason: Per HR records, employee E003 (Alexandra Johnson) is a full-time Analyst. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and Analyst does not own it, so per policy full-time employees max out at write (admin only if their role owns the system). Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so grant the maximum: write. (Note: Security's note lists the employee as contractor with basic training, but HR is the authoritative source for employment type; either way admin is not permitted, and the granted level is the full-time maximum.)
